question: A 55-year-old patient is diagnosed with pemphigus vulgaris and has extensive cutaneous erosions with worsening oral involvement. Which management approach is most appropriate?

answers.text: High-dose systemic corticosteroids (e.g. prednisolone ~1 mg/kg/day) combined early with a steroid-sparing immunosuppressant such as azathioprine, plus supportive wound care

tipsAndFeedback.chosenFeedback: Correct. Pemphigus vulgaris is the more aggressive autoimmune blistering disease and requires high-dose systemic corticosteroids combined early with a steroid-sparing agent (azathioprine, mycophenolate, or cyclophosphamide) to enable eventual steroid tapering. Supportive wound care is essential alongside immunosuppression.

answers.text: Potent topical corticosteroid cream alone, with outpatient review in six weeks

tipsAndFeedback.chosenFeedback: Topical corticosteroids alone are insufficient for pemphigus vulgaris with extensive erosions. The autoantibodies circulate systemically, so systemic immunosuppression is required. A six-week review risks dangerous progression, fluid loss, and sepsis.

answers.text: Immediate rituximab infusion in the emergency department without specialist assessment

tipsAndFeedback.chosenFeedback: Rituximab is increasingly used as early targeted therapy for PV, but it is a specialist decision requiring dermatological assessment, staging, screening for contraindications, and monitoring — not a casualty-initiated intervention.

answers.text: Oral antihistamines and emollients, as pemphigus vulgaris is self-limiting

tipsAndFeedback.chosenFeedback: Pemphigus vulgaris is not self-limiting — untreated, it has historically been fatal. Antihistamines and emollients address neither the autoimmune process nor the life-threatening risks of fluid loss and secondary infection from extensive erosions.

overallFeedback.feedback: Pemphigus vulgaris needs high-dose systemic corticosteroids (~1 mg/kg/day prednisolone) combined early with a steroid-sparing immunosuppressant such as azathioprine. Topical therapy alone is inadequate, and untreated disease can be fatal.
Correct — pemphigus vulgaris requires aggressive systemic immunosuppression with early addition of a steroid-sparing agent, alongside supportive wound care.
